subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram channel_post commands, should a configured groups[chatId].allowFrom sender allowlist be ignored in favor of explicit chat allow, or should channel_post fail closed as unsupported when sender-scoped auth is configured?
rationale: This is an authorization boundary on a Telegram update type where the normal human sender may be absent, and current code/docs do not establish the intended security semantics.

options.title: Fail Closed When Sender Auth Is Configured
options.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document the limitation until a stronger identity model exists.

options.title: Allow Explicit Chat Only
options.body: Permit channel_post commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that sender-scoped allowFrom is intentionally ignored on this surface.

options.title: Fold Into Bot-To-Bot Policy
options.body: Pause this narrow decision until broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work defines peer-bot and channel identity semantics together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed When Sender Auth Is Configured
recommendation.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands, return a clear denial or diagnostic, and document the limitation until a stronger identity model exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current-main history ties this owner to shared group-access code and Telegram docs where the policy would likely be encoded.
